name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
contribution: The last Shah of Iran, reigning from 1941 to 1979 as the second monarch of the Pahlavi dynasty.
legacy: This person's legacy remains divisive, reflecting his authoritarian rule, political repression, human rights violations, and close alignment with Western powers, alongside his efforts to modernize Iran's economy and enhance its geopolitical influence.

checks.lead: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi (26 October 1919 – 27 July 1980) was the last Shah of Iran, reigning from 1941 to 1979 as the second monarch of the Pahlavi dynasty. He succeeded his father, Reza Shah, and ruled the Imperial State of Iran until his overthrow in the Islamic Revolution, which abolished the nearly 2,500-year-old Iranian monarchy. During his reign, he assumed the title Shahanshah (lit. 'King of Kings'), and held several other titles, including Aryamehr (lit. 'Light of the Aryans') and Bozorg Arteshtaran (lit. 'Grand Army Commander').
